newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU INCHES DOWN, MONEY MARKET RATES UP.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU INCHES DOWN, MONEY MARKET RATES UP.

text.p: The Romanian leu currency crawled down to 5,700/750 to the dollar on Friday after idling at 5,650/720 throughout the day on an interbank market faced by months-long hard currency shortages.
"Trading stayed thin, with hard currency sellers still in a wait-and-see attitude," said one trader.
Latest central bank data showed a $158,100 interbank volume on Thursday, when overall trading was $17.9 million.
The leu softened by 7.0 percent against the greenback this week, compared with last week's 23.4 percent fall -- its sharpest weekly drop in a year.

But the leu's downswing slowed over the past two days, with the currency gaining some support from a central bank move to tighten its monetary policies again by lifting its one-week rate to 70 percent from 65 percent.
Traders were reluctant to give a forecast for the leu's future trend against the background of inflationary fears.
"It's very hard to say what could happen before we have clues about the package tackled with the Fund," said one trader.

Earlier this week the International Monetary Fund started talks with Romania's new centrist ruling coalition on resuming IMF credits suspended last year. Negotiations are expected to take up to three weeks.
Leu-dollar retail rates stayed near 6,200/450 on Friday when they were some 9.0 percent down from last week's close.
Short-term rates climbed to 55-57 percent against 50 percent earlier in the week with the money market reacting to to the surge in the central bank's one-week rate.
Traders said big players had also started to chase funds following a cut by 350 billion to 750 billion lei in the central bank's offer of one-week refinancing funds.
